findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
findings.body: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), the new code calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments. However, the only method that exists in UsernamePasswordForm (which UsernameForm extends) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no zero-argument overload, so this is a compile error and the PR cannot be built. The intended call is almost certainly `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` — without the argument the method body would have referenced an undefined symbol, and even if it compiled it would still need the UserModel to check `user != null` correctly.

findings.title: Awkward try/catch/fail pattern instead of assertThrows
findings.body: In the new `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test, the assertions that no `form[@id='webauth']` element exists use an inverted try/catch/fail pattern: `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...)`. This catches any Exception (including NoSuchElementException, AssertionError, runtime errors) and treats them all as success. If the page happens to change in the future so that findElement throws something else, or returns a non-null WebElement that fails the null check, the test silently swallows it. The existing project convention (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest line 202, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest before the change) is to use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")))`. The same issue appears at line 313 in this file.

findings.title: Public/protected API surface: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled signature is unusual
findings.body: The new helper `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` mixes responsibilities: the method name suggests a configuration check, but its body also requires the user to be non-null. Callers must always pass `context.getUser()` rather than the more natural `null` when querying the realm-level toggle. This will cause subtle bugs in future callers (e.g. someone calling `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null)` to ask "are passkeys enabled in this realm?" will get false even when they are). Consider splitting into two methods (e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` for the realm-level check and `isConditionalPasskeysAvailableFor(UserModel user)` for the combined check) or rename to make the semantics clear.

findings.title: Stale inline comment after refactor
findings.body: The comment on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH field still reads "In this case we skip clearing of the user after unsuccessful password authentication", which is fine, but the inlined `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` call in `badPasswordHandler` no longer carries its own explanatory comment. Given that the helper now also affects the re-authentication form layout (USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED), callers may not realize the side-effect. A short Javadoc on `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` documenting what form attributes it sets and why would help — currently the Javadoc is just an implementation comment.
